have already been the subject of notices given under subsection 26BD(5) of the Act; and
have not been finally determined;
then a decision on whether to make a recommendation on the current application must be made within the period of:
if the current application is an IN1 application—70 working days beginning on the later of the start day and the day the evaluation fee is paid for the current application; or
if the current application is an IN2 application—120 working days beginning on the later of the start day and the day the evaluation fee is paid for the current application; or
if the current application is an IN3 application—150 working days beginning on the later of the start day and the day the evaluation fee is paid for the current application; or
if the current application is an IN4 application—180 working days beginning on the later of the start day and the day the evaluation fee is paid for the current application.
(1B) For the purposes of this regulation, the start day is:
the day after all the related applications have been finally determined, unless paragraph (b) applies; or
if a determination is made under subsection 26BB(1) of the Act in relation to the ingredient—the day on which that determination commences.

(1C) For the purposes of this regulation, an application is finally determined when the application, and any applications for review or appeals arising out of it, have been finally determined or otherwise disposed of.

A failure to make a decision on whether to make a recommendation on an application within the period applicable under this regulation does not make the Commonwealth, the Secretary or a delegate of the Secretary liable to a person for loss, damage or injury, of any kind, that is caused by or arises out of the failure.

section.heading: Period for paying evaluation fee for application under subsection 26BD(1) of the Act

content.p: For the purposes of paragraph 26BDA(c) of the Act, the period is the period of 2 months beginning on the day that the applicant is notified of the amount of the evaluation fee and of the requirement for that fee to be paid.

section.heading: Determination of competent regulatory authority of a foreign country or foreign jurisdiction in relation to evaluation of applications

content.p: The Secretary may, in writing published on the Therapeutic Goods Administration website, determine a competent regulatory authority of a foreign country or a foreign jurisdiction in relation to the evaluation of the following medicine applications:
an IN1 application;
an IN2 application;
an IN3 application;
an L(A)2 application;
an RCM2 application;
an RCM3 application;
an RCM4 application.

section.heading: Application to designate medicine as orphan drug

content.p: The sponsor of a medicine may apply to the Secretary to designate, in writing, the medicine as an orphan drug.
An application under subregulation (1) must be in a form approved, in writing, by the Secretary.

section.heading: Designation of medicine as orphan drug

content.p: On receiving an application under subregulation 16H(1) to designate a medicine as an orphan drug, the Secretary must:
consider the application; and
decide either:
to designate the medicine as an orphan drug; or
to refuse to designate the medicine as an orphan drug.
The Secretary may decide to designate the medicine as an orphan drug if the Secretary is satisfied, having regard to any matter that the Secretary considers relevant, that:
if the medicine is not a new dosage form medicine—all of the criteria specified in subregulation (3) are satisfied in relation to the medicine; or
if the medicine is a new dosage form medicine—all of the criteria specified in subregulation (4) are satisfied in relation to the medicine.
General criteria
The following criteria are specified in relation to a medicine that is not a new dosage form medicine:
the application is for only one indication of the medicine;
(b) the indication is the treatment, prevention or diagnosis of a life-threatening or seriously debilitating condition in a particular class of patients (the relevant patient class);
it is not medically plausible that the medicine could effectively treat, prevent or diagnose the condition in another class of patients that is not covered by the relevant patient class;
at least one of the following applies:
if the medicine is intended to treat the condition—the condition affects fewer than 5 in 10,000 individuals in Australia when the application is made;

if the medicine is intended to prevent or diagnose the condition—the medicine, if it were included in the Register, would not be likely to be supplied to more than 5 in 10,000 individuals in Australia during each year that it is included in the Register;
it is not likely to be financially viable for the sponsor to market the medicine in Australia unless each fee referred to in paragraph 45(12)(c) were waived in relation to the medicine;
none of the following has refused to approve the medicine for the treatment, prevention or diagnosis of the condition for a reason relating to the medicine’s safety:
the Secretary;
the United States Food and Drug Administration;
the European Medicines Agency;
Health Canada;
the Medicines and Healthcare products Regulatory Agency of the United Kingdom;
either:

no therapeutic goods that are intended to treat, prevent or diagnose the condition are included in the Register (except in the part of the Register for goods known as provisionally registered goods); or

if one or more therapeutic goods that are intended to treat, prevent or diagnose the condition are included in the Register (except in the part of the Register for goods known as provisionally registered goods)—the medicine provides a significant benefit in relation to the efficacy or safety of the treatment, prevention or diagnosis of the condition, or a major contribution to patient care, compared to those goods.
New dosage form medicines
The following criteria are specified in relation to a new dosage form medicine:
the application is for only one indication of the medicine;
the indication is the treatment, prevention or diagnosis of a life-threatening or seriously debilitating condition;
it is not likely to be financially viable for the sponsor to market the medicine in Australia unless each fee referred to in paragraph 45(12)(c) were waived in relation to the medicine;
none of the following has refused to approve the medicine for the treatment, prevention or diagnosis of the condition for a reason relating to the medicine’s safety:
the Secretary;
the United States Food and Drug Administration;
the European Medicines Agency;
Health Canada;
the Medicines and Healthcare products Regulatory Agency of the United Kingdom;
either:

no therapeutic goods that are intended to treat, prevent or diagnose the condition are included in the Register (except in the part of the Register for goods known as provisionally registered goods); or

if one or more therapeutic goods that are intended to treat, prevent or diagnose the condition are included in the Register (except in the part of the Register for goods known as provisionally registered goods)—the medicine provides a significant benefit in relation to the efficacy or safety of the treatment, prevention or diagnosis of the condition, or a major contribution to patient care, compared to those goods.
Publication of decision

If the Secretary decides to designate the medicine as an orphan drug, the Secretary must, as soon as practicable after making the decision, publish a notice on the Department’s website stating the following:
the name of the sponsor of the medicine;
the indication referred to in paragraph (3)(a) or (4)(a);
the dosage form of the medicine;
that the medicine is a designated orphan drug.
Notification of decision
As soon as practicable after making the decision, the Secretary must notify the applicant, in writing, of the decision.
If the Secretary decides to refuse to make the designation, the notification must include the reasons for the decision.

section.heading: Period during which designation is in force

content.p: A designation under regulation 16J of a medicine as an orphan drug:
comes into force when it is made; and
remains in force for a period of 6 months.
Subregulation (1) has effect subject to regulations 16L and 16M.
If a designation under regulation 16J of a medicine as an orphan drug is in force, the sponsor of the medicine may apply to the Secretary to extend the designation for a further 6 months.
An application under subregulation (1) to extend a designation must:
be in a form approved, in writing, by the Secretary; and
be made at least 28 days before the designation would cease to be in force.
On receiving an application under subregulation (1) to extend a designation, the Secretary must decide either:
to extend the designation; or
to refuse to extend the designation.
The Secretary may extend the designation if:
the Secretary has not previously extended the designation; and
the Secretary is satisfied that:
if the medicine is not a new dosage form medicine—the criteria specified in paragraphs 16J(3)(e) and (f) are satisfied in relation to the medicine; or
if the medicine is a new dosage form medicine—the criteria specified in paragraphs 16J(4)(d) and (e) are satisfied in relation to the medicine; and

the Secretary is satisfied that, if the Secretary were to extend the designation, the sponsor would make an application in relation to the medicine under section 23 of the Act before the end of the extended designation.
Notification of decision
As soon as practicable after making the decision, the Secretary must notify the applicant, in writing, of the decision.
If the Secretary decides to refuse to extend the designation, the notification must include the reasons for the decision.
The Secretary may, by written notice given to the sponsor of a designated orphan drug, revoke the designation:
on application by the sponsor; or
if the Secretary is satisfied that:
if the designated orphan drug is a new dosage form medicine—the criteria specified in subregulation 16J(4) are no longer satisfied in relation to the designated orphan drug; or
if the designated orphan drug is not a new dosage form medicine—the criteria specified in subregulation 16J(3) are no longer satisfied in relation to the designated orphan drug.
(2) Subsection 33(3) of the Acts Interpretation Act 1901 does not apply in relation to a revocation of a designation under regulation 16J of a medicine as an orphan drug.
For the purposes of subsection 25AAA(1) of the Act, this Part makes provision for and in relation to the making of a therapeutic goods (priority applicant) determination in relation to a medicine.

section.heading: Application for therapeutic goods (priority applicant) determination

content.p: A person may apply to the Secretary for a therapeutic goods (priority applicant) determination in relation to a medicine.
An application under subregulation (1) must:
be in writing; and
be in a form approved, in writing, by the Secretary; and
have with it written information in such detail as is reasonably necessary to allow the application to be properly considered.
An application under subregulation (1) is taken not to have been made unless:
the application meets the requirements in subregulation (2); and
subject to paragraph 45(12)(d), the fee prescribed in item 1B of Part 2 of Schedule 9 for making the application has been paid.
Note: Paragraph 45(12)(d) provides that the Secretary must waive the fee for applying for a therapeutic goods (priority applicant) determination in certain circumstances.

section.heading: Making of therapeutic goods (priority applicant) determination

content.p: On receiving an application under subregulation 16Q(1) for a therapeutic goods (priority applicant) determination in relation to a medicine, the Secretary must:
consider the application; and
decide either:
to make the determination; or
to refuse to make the determination.
Criteria

The Secretary may make the determination if the Secretary is satisfied, having regard to any matter that the Secretary considers relevant, that all of the following criteria are satisfied in relation to the medicine:
the medicine is:
a new prescription medicine; or
a new indications medicine;
(b) an indication of the medicine (the priority indication) is the treatment, prevention or diagnosis of a life-threatening or seriously debilitating condition;
either:

no therapeutic goods that are intended to treat, prevent or diagnose the condition are included in the Register (except in the part of the Register for goods known as provisionally registered goods); or

if one or more therapeutic goods that are intended to treat, prevent or diagnose the condition are included in the Register (except in the part of the Register for goods known as provisionally registered goods)—there is substantial evidence demonstrating that the medicine provides a significant improvement in the efficacy or safety of the treatment, prevention or diagnosis of the condition compared to those goods;
there is substantial evidence demonstrating that the medicine provides a major therapeutic advance.

Note: Paragraph 16(1)(e) of the Act provides that, for the purposes of Part 3-2 of the Act, therapeutic goods (other than medicine of the kind to which subsection 16(1A) of the Act applies) are to be taken to be separate and distinct from other therapeutic goods if they have different indications.
Information to be specified in determination
The determination must specify:
the person who, as a result of section 25AAA of the Act, is the priority applicant; and
each active ingredient of the medicine to which the determination relates; and
the priority indication of the medicine.
Notification of decision
As soon as practicable after making the decision, the Secretary must notify the applicant, in writing, of the decision.
If the Secretary decides to refuse to make the determination, the notification must include the reasons for the decision.

section.heading: Period during which therapeutic goods (priority applicant) determination is in force

content.p: A therapeutic goods (priority applicant) determination in relation to a medicine:
comes into force on the day on which the Secretary notifies the priority applicant in accordance with subregulation 16R(4); and
subject to subregulation (2) and regulation 16T, remains in force for 6 months.

If the priority applicant specified in the determination makes an application under section 23 of the Act for the registration of the medicine that passes preliminary assessment before the end of the 6 month period beginning when the determination comes into force, the determination remains in force until:
the priority applicant withdraws the application; or
the application lapses in accordance with subsection 24(2) of the Act; or
the priority applicant gives the Secretary written notice under subsection 24E(2) of the Act that the applicant wishes to treat the application as having been refused; or
the application is finally determined.
Note: See subsection 23B(3) of the Act for when an application passes preliminary assessment.

section.heading: Revocation of therapeutic goods (priority applicant) determination

content.p: The Secretary may revoke a therapeutic goods (priority applicant) determination in relation to a medicine if:
either:
the priority applicant specified in the determination has not made an application under section 23 of the Act for the registration of the medicine; or
the priority applicant has made such an application, but the application does not pass preliminary assessment; and
the Secretary is satisfied that the criteria specified in subregulation 16R(2) are no longer satisfied in relation to the medicine.
Note: See subsection 23B(3) of the Act for when an application passes preliminary assessment.
The revocation must be by written notice given by the Secretary to the priority applicant.
For the purposes of subsection 32DEA(1) of the Act, this Part makes provision for and in relation to the making of biologicals (priority applicant) determinations.
A person may apply to the Secretary for a biologicals (priority applicant) determination in relation to a biological, other than a Class 1 biological or an export only biological.
An application under subregulation (1) must:
be in writing; and
be in a form approved, in writing, by the Secretary; and
have with it written information in such detail as is reasonably necessary to allow the application to be properly considered.
An application under subregulation (1) is taken to not have been made unless:
the application meets the requirements in subregulation (2); and
the fee prescribed in item 2A in Part 2 of Schedule 9A for making the application has been paid.
On receiving an application under subregulation 16V(1) for a biologicals (priority applicant) determination in relation to a biological, the Secretary must:
consider the application; and
decide either:
to make the determination; or
to refuse to make the determination.
Criteria

The Secretary may make the determination if the Secretary is satisfied, having regard to any matter that the Secretary considers relevant, that all of the following criteria are satisfied in relation to the biological:
the biological is separate and distinct from biologicals included in the Register;
either:
(i) for a Class 2 biological—an intended clinical use (the priority indication) of the biological is the treatment, prevention or diagnosis of a life-threating or seriously debilitating condition; or

(ii) for a Class 3 or Class 4 biological—a therapeutic indication (the priority indication) of the biological is the treatment, prevention or diagnosis of a life-threatening or seriously debilitating condition;
either:

no therapeutic goods that are intended to treat, prevent or diagnose the condition are included in the Register (except in the part of the Register for goods known as provisionally registered goods); or

if one or more therapeutic goods that are intended to treat, prevent or diagnose the condition are included in the Register (except in the part of the Register for goods known as provisionally registered goods)—there is substantial evidence demonstrating that the biological provides a significant improvement in the efficacy or safety of the treatment, prevention or diagnosis of the condition compared to those goods;
there is substantial evidence demonstrating that the biological provides a major therapeutic advance.
Note: For paragraph (a), see section 32AB of the Act and regulation 11A for when a biological is separate and distinct from other biologicals.
Information to be specified in the determination
The determination must specify:
the person who, as a result of section 32DEA of the Act, is the priority applicant; and
each active ingredient of the biological to which the determination relates; and
the priority indication of the biological.
Notification of decision
As soon as practicable after making the decision, the Secretary must notify the applicant, in writing, of the decision.
If the Secretary decides to refuse to make the determination, the notification must include the reasons for the decision.

section.heading: Period during which biologicals (priority applicant) determination is in force

content.p: A biologicals (priority applicant) determination in relation to a biological:
comes into force on the day on which the Secretary notifies the priority applicant in accordance with subregulation 16W(4); and
subject to subregulation (2) and regulation 16Y, remains in force for 6 months.

If the priority applicant specified in the determination makes an application under section 32DD of the Act to include the biological in the Register that passes preliminary assessment before the end of the 6 month period beginning when the determination comes into force, the determination remains in force until:
the priority applicant withdraws the application; or
the application lapses in accordance with section 32DH of the Act; or
the application is finally determined.
Note: See subsection 32DDA(3) of the Act for when an application passes preliminary assessment.
The Secretary may revoke a biologicals (priority applicant) determination in relation to a biological if:
either:
the priority applicant specified in the determination has not made an application under section 32DD of the Act to include the biological in the Register; or
the priority applicant has made such an application, but the application does not pass preliminary assessment; and
the Secretary is satisfied that the criteria specified in subregulation 16W(2) are no longer satisfied in relation to the biological.
Note: See subsection 32DDA(3) of the Act for when an application passes preliminary assessment.
The revocation must be by written notice given by the Secretary to the priority applicant.

section.heading: Exempt goods for the purposes of subsection 34(1) of the Act

content.p: For the purposes of subsection 34(1) of the Act, the therapeutic goods specified in Schedule 7 are exempt from the operation of Part 3-3 of the Act unless the goods are supplied as pharmaceutical benefits.
If:
therapeutic goods that are exempt from the operation of Part 3-3 of the Act cease to be exempt; and

before the day on which the goods cease to be exempt, each person who carries out a step in the manufacture of the goods applies for a licence authorising the person to carry out the step on premises referred to in the application;
the goods produced by those persons carrying out the steps on those premises are taken to be exempt from the operation of that Part until each application is determined.

For the purposes of subsection 34(2) of the Act, the persons specified in column 2 of an item in Schedule 8 are exempt from the operation of Part 3-3 of the Act in relation to the manufacture, or the steps in the manufacture, of the therapeutic goods specified in column 3 of that item.

For the purposes of section 40 of the Act, it is a condition of each licence that the licence holder must give the Secretary, at the time of payment of the annual licensing charge in respect of the licence:

if the Secretary so requests—details of therapeutic goods manufactured by or on behalf of the licence holder during the period of 12 months immediately preceding the date on which the payment of the charge is due; and
the name, qualifications and details of the relevant experience of any person nominated by the licence holder as having control of:
the production of the goods; and
the quality control measures that are to be employed in the manufacture of the goods.
For the purposes of section 40 of the Act, the following are conditions to which each licence is subject:
a copy of the licence and of any document issued by the Secretary imposing or amending the conditions applicable to that licence are to be displayed publicly at the premises specified in the licence;
unless the contrary intention appears in the licence or in documents issued by the Secretary imposing or amending the conditions applicable to the licence, the licence holder must:
keep records showing:
(A) the materials used in the manufacture of the goods, the supplier and quantities of the materials used and details of the tests performed on those materials; and
(B) the procedures and controls employed in the manufacture of the goods, including the results of tests carried out during the processing of the goods; and
(C) details of the tests performed on the goods and the results of those tests; and
(D) the stability studies (if any) that validate the recommended shelf life and appropriate storage conditions of the goods; and
where the goods to which the licence relates are produced in identifiable batches:
(A) assign a batch number to each batch of the goods; and

(B) if it is not unreasonable in the circumstances—retain at those premises, for not less than 12 months after the expiry date of the goods or, if there is no expiry date, for not less than 6 years after completion of manufacture of the goods, a sample of each batch of the finished goods; and

retain those records at the licensed premises for at least 12 months after the expiry date of the goods to which they relate or, if there is no expiry date, for not less than 6 years after completion of manufacture of the goods; and

ensure that the persons nominated by the licence holder as having control of the production of the goods and of the quality control measures that are to be employed in the manufacture of the goods maintain that control.

section.heading: Persons having control of production etc to be named

content.p: If:

an applicant for a licence to manufacture therapeutic goods nominates a person as having control of the production of goods or the quality control measures in respect of the manufacture of the goods; and
the licence is granted; and
the applicant wishes to replace the nominated person with another person;
then it is a condition of the licence that the licence holder must inform the Secretary as soon as practicable of the name, qualifications and experience of that other person.
If a person who was the holder of a licence dies, the legal personal representative of the dead person:
is taken to be the holder of the licence; and
must notify the Secretary, in writing, of the death not later than 3 months after it occurred.
If a person who is the holder of a licence becomes bankrupt, the trustee in bankruptcy of the estate of the bankrupt:
is taken to be the holder of the licence; and
must notify the Secretary, in writing, of the bankruptcy not later than 3 months after the person became bankrupt.
If a body corporate that is the holder of a licence is being wound up, the liquidator of the body corporate:
is taken to be the holder of the licence; and
must, not later than 3 months after the body corporate is wound up, notify the Secretary, in writing, of the winding up.
If:
a person agrees to dispose of a business relating to the manufacture, distribution or sale of therapeutic goods; and
it is agreed that the disposal of that business is to include a transfer of a licence held by that person;
then:
the person who acquires that business is taken to be the holder of the licence; and
that person must, not later than 3 months after the transfer, notify the Secretary that the person has, by reason of that agreement, become an applicant for the licence.
If a person who is the holder of a licence:
changes his, her or its name; or
being a corporation, amalgamates with another corporation under a name that is different from the name of the holder of the licence;
the person must give notice in writing to the Secretary of the new name of the person, and the circumstance giving rise to it, within 3 months after the occurrence of the circumstance.
The licence has effect as if it had been granted to the holder in the holder’s new name.

When a person notifies the Secretary of an event referred to in paragraph (1)(b), (2)(b), (3)(b), (4)(d) or (4A)(a) or (b), the person must send to the Secretary sufficient documentary evidence to establish the matter asserted in the notification.

When a person is taken to be the holder of a licence in accordance with this regulation, the Secretary may regard the person as an applicant for the licence and may deal with the notification referred to in paragraph (1)(b), (2)(b), (3)(b), (4)(d) or (4A)(a) or (b) as if it were an application for a licence.

In spite of subregulation (6), a person who is regarded as an applicant for a licence because of the operation of that subsection may continue to manufacture therapeutic goods under the original licence until the application is determined.

If, at any time, the Secretary becomes aware that he or she has not been informed in accordance with this regulation of an event referred to in paragraph (1)(b), (2)(b), (3)(b), (4)(d) or (4A)(a) or (b), the Secretary may cancel the licence to which the event relates.
This Part is made for the purposes of subsection 63(1) and paragraphs 63(2)(d) and (g) of the Act.
This Part does not preclude the testing of goods other than under this Part.

(1) An APS employee in the Department is an analyst for the purposes of performing functions and duties, or exercising powers, under this Part, if the Secretary nominates the APS employee, in writing, under this subregulation.

The Secretary may only nominate a person under subregulation (1) if the Secretary is satisfied that the person has appropriate qualifications, experience or knowledge to perform those functions and duties or exercise those powers.

An analyst may select a sample of goods for testing under this regulation for the purpose of the administration of the Act, regulations made under the Act, or an instrument made under the Act or those regulations, including (but not limited to) testing for any the following purposes:
ascertaining whether or not the goods are therapeutic goods or vaping goods;
assessing the quality, safety, efficacy or performance of therapeutic goods or vaping goods;
monitoring or investigating compliance or non-compliance with the Act, regulations made under the Act, or an instrument made under the Act or those regulations;
supporting the enforcement of the Act, regulations made under the Act, or an instrument made under the Act or those regulations.
If an analyst selects a sample of goods for testing under this regulation, the analyst must:
test the sample or arrange for another analyst to test the sample; or
arrange for the sample to be tested by another appropriate person or body.

Note: An analyst, a person who conducts a test on a sample of goods under an arrangement under paragraph (b), a person assisting the analyst or other person, and a person with whom an arrangement is made under paragraph (b), are protected persons for the purposes of section 61A (immunity from civil actions) and section 62 (protection from criminal responsibility) of the Act: see regulation 46B and those sections of the Act.

However if, after a sample of goods is selected for testing (whether or not the testing has commenced or an arrangement has been made under paragraph (2)(b)), an analyst decides it is no longer appropriate, possible or necessary for the sample to be tested:
the sample is not required to be tested under this regulation; and
if testing of the sample has already commenced—the testing may be ceased.
A sample of goods may be tested under this regulation:
regardless of how or where the sample was obtained or accessed by, or given to:
the Department or an analyst; or
another person or body as arranged under paragraph (2)(b); and
whether or not the goods are registered, listed or included in the Register.
To avoid doubt:
more than one test may be conducted on a particular sample of goods; and
more than one analyst or other person or body may test a particular sample of goods; and
a particular sample of goods may be tested at more than one place.
A reference in this regulation to a sample of goods includes a reference to a part of a sample of goods.
Analyst to issue certificate
If a sample of goods is tested under regulation 25 (including as arranged under paragraph 25(2)(b)), an analyst must issue a certificate setting out:
the test that was conducted; and
the results of the testing.
The certificate may also set out other information relating to the sample or the testing of the sample.
The certificate may cover:
more than one test conducted on the sample; and
tests conducted on the sample by different analysts or other persons or bodies; and
tests conducted on the sample at different places.
More than one certificate may be issued under subregulation (1) in relation to a particular sample.
Providing certificate to certain persons

If the goods from which the sample was taken are registered, listed or included in the Register, an analyst must cause a copy of the certificate to be given to the person in relation to whom the goods are so registered, listed or included.
Use of certificate in proceedings
In:
proceedings for an offence against the Act (see subsection 3(7) of the Act) or a contravention of a civil penalty provision; or
any other proceedings under the Act or regulations made under the Act;
a certificate issued under subregulation (1) of this regulation is prima facie evidence of the matters set out in the certificate.
Document purporting to be certificate

A document purporting to be a certificate issued under subregulation (1) or a copy of that certificate is, unless evidence to the contrary is adduced, taken to be such a certificate or copy and to have been duly given.
References to a sample of goods
A reference in this regulation to a sample of goods includes a reference to a part of a sample of goods.

section.heading: Prescribed circumstances under which biologicals may be imported, exported or supplied

content.p: For paragraphs 14(5A)(b), (9A)(b), (13A)(b), 14A(1A)(b), (2A)(b) and (3A)(b) of the Act, the circumstances are:
the patient has been clinically assessed by the treating medical practitioner to require the biological urgently to treat a serious condition; and

a biological that is included in the Register under Part 3-2A of the Act and conforms with the applicable manufacturing requirements and standards is not available, or is not available within the time necessary for treatment to occur; and
a nonconforming biological that is included in the Register under Part 3-2A of the Act is available; and
no other treatment option is suitable for the patient; and
the nonconforming biological is assessed as the most suitable treatment for the patient; and
the nonconforming biological is to be used only for the treatment of one patient.
For subsection 15AB(1) of the Act, the conditions are that:
all the circumstances mentioned in regulation 33A have occurred; and
the sponsor of the nonconforming biological mentioned in paragraph 33A(c) receives from the treating medical practitioner a copy of a written statement of the following:
the proposal to use the nonconforming biological;
that the patient or guardian has been told about the likely risks and benefits from the use of the biological;
why the biological is nonconforming with standards applicable to the biological or was not manufactured in accordance with relevant manufacturing principles under section 36 of the Act; and
the medical or scientific director of the sponsor’s facility from which the supply of the biological is to occur must give written approval for release of the biological; and
before the biological is used:
the patient or the patient’s guardian must give written informed consent; or
the treating medical practitioner must give written statement of the reasons that consent cannot be given; and
the consent and the approval must be placed on the patient’s medical records and a copy must be given to the treating medical practitioner.
Within 28 days after the release of the nonconforming biological, the sponsor must give to the Secretary:
a notification of use of the nonconforming biological, on a form approved by the Secretary; and
a copy of the documents mentioned in paragraphs (1)(b) to (d); and
any other information requested by the Secretary, including any information requested after submission of the notification.
The Secretary must give the sponsor written acknowledgement of the receipt of the notification within 28 days after receiving the notification and any further information requested by the Secretary.

section.heading: Report on release of nonconforming biological

content.p: For each nonconforming biological released from a cell or tissue bank, the sponsor of the nonconforming biological must give to the Secretary:
within 6 months after the release—a report that includes the following information:
date of release;
product identification details;
name and address of transplant centre or medical practitioner to whom the nonconforming biological was released;
initials, gender and date of birth of patient;
any adverse events relating to the use of the nonconforming biological; and
within 14 days after a request by the Secretary—information about the supply of the nonconforming biological and the circumstances surrounding the supply, including:
the decision making process leading to the supply; and
any adverse events related to the supply.

division.heading: Advisory Committee on Medicines

content.p: The Advisory Committee on Medicines is established.
The committee’s functions are, at the request of the Minister or Secretary, to provide advice and to make recommendations to the Minister or Secretary about one or more of the following matters:
the safety, quality and efficacy of medicines, including in relation to pharmacovigilance;
the entry of a medicine in the Register;
the variation of an entry for a medicine in the Register;
the continued retention of a medicine in, or the removal of a medicine from, the Register;
risk assessment and risk management of medicines;
the repurposing of medicines under the program known as the Medicines Repurposing Program;
any other matter (whether or not related to a medicine), including a matter related to standards.
The Minister or Secretary may require the committee to give its advice to other persons or bodies.
The Minister may appoint, in writing, up to 20 persons to the committee in accordance with subregulations (1A) and (1B).
Subject to subregulation (1B):
to the extent reasonably practicable, membership of the committee is to represent the widest possible range of fields mentioned in subregulation (2); and
each member of the committee must have expertise in at least one of those fields.
One member of the committee may have expertise in consumer health issues.
For the purposes of subregulation (1A), the fields are as follows:
general medical practice in Australia;
specialist medical practice of a kind that is relevant to the committee’s functions;
epidemiology or biostatistics;
clinical pharmacology or pharmacokinetics;
paediatrics;
gerontology;
internal medicine, including the following:
haematology;
oncology;
infectious diseases;
cardiology;
gastroenterology or hepatology;
renal disease;
endocrinology;
neurology;
immunology;
rheumatology;
respiratory disease;
intensive care;
anaesthetics;
psychiatry;
toxicology;
pharmaceutical chemistry;
microbiology;
community or clinical pharmacy;
manufacture of medicines;
dermatology;
obstetrics or gynaecology;
ophthalmology;
radiology;
medical genetics;
developmental or reproductive toxicology;
medicines in pregnancy;
medical ethics.

division.heading: Advisory Committee on Medical Devices

content.p: The Advisory Committee on Medical Devices is established.
The committee’s functions are, at the request of the Minister or Secretary, to provide advice and to make recommendations to the Minister or Secretary about one or more of the following matters:
the safety, performance and manufacturing of a medical device;
the inclusion of a medical device or other therapeutic goods in the Register;
the variation of an entry for a medical device or other therapeutic goods in the Register;
the continued retention of a medical device or other therapeutic good in, or the removal of a medical device or other therapeutic good from, the Register;
risk assessment and risk management of medical devices;
any other matter (whether or not related to a medical device or other therapeutic goods).
The Minister or Secretary may require the committee to give its advice to other persons or bodies.
The Minister may appoint, in writing, up to 16 persons to the committee in accordance with subregulations (2) and (3).
Subject to subregulation (3):
to the extent reasonably practicable, membership of the committee is to represent the widest possible range of fields mentioned in subregulations (4) and (5); and
each member of the committee must have either or both of the following:
medical or surgical expertise in one of the fields mentioned in subregulation (4);
expertise in at least one of the fields mentioned in subregulation (5).
One member of the committee may have expertise in consumer health issues.
For the purposes of paragraph (2)(a) and subparagraph (2)(b)(i), the fields are as follows:
anaesthetics;
cardiology;
cardiothoracic surgery;
dentistry or oro-maxillofacial surgery;
ear, nose and throat;
gastroenterology;
neurology;
obstetrics or gynaecology;
ophthalmology;
orthopaedics;
pathology;
plastic and reconstructive surgery;
renal;
respiratory medicine;
vascular medicine;
any other medical or surgical field of expertise that is relevant to the committee’s functions.
For the purposes of paragraph (2)(a) and subparagraph (2)(b)(ii), the fields are as follows:
biomedical engineering or biomaterials;
epidemiology or biostatistics;
general medical practice in Australia;
human factors analysis;
interventional cardiology;
interventional radiology;
manufacture of medical devices;
medical device software engineering;
nursing;
any other clinical or technical field of expertise that is relevant to the committee’s functions.

division.heading: Advisory Committee on Complementary Medicines

content.p: The Advisory Committee on Complementary Medicines is established.
The committee’s functions are, at the request of the Minister or Secretary, to provide advice and to make recommendations to the Minister or Secretary about one or more of the following matters:
the safety, efficacy and manufacturing quality of a complementary medicine;
the safety and quality of ingredients that are, or are proposed to be, included in a determination under subsection 26BB(1) of the Act for a listed complementary medicine;
any requirements that are, or are proposed to be, included in a determination under subsection 26BB(1) of the Act in relation to ingredients for a listed complementary medicine;
the registration or listing of a complementary medicine;
the variation of an entry for a complementary medicine in the Register;
the continued retention of a complementary medicine in, or the removal of a complementary medicine from, the Register;
any other matter (whether or not related to a complementary medicine), including a matter related to standards.
The Minister or Secretary may require the committee to give its advice to other persons or bodies.
The minister may appoint, in writing, up to 8 persons to the committee in accordance with subregulations (1A) and (1B).
Subject to subregulation (1B):
to the extent reasonably practicable, membership of the committee is to represent the widest possible range of fields mentioned in subregulation (2); and
each member of the committee must have expertise in at least one of those fields.
One member of the committee may have expertise in consumer health issues.
For the purposes of subregulation (1A), the fields are as follows:
complementary medical practice;
manufacture of medicines;
general medical practice in Australia;
herbal medicine;
naturopathy;
nutrition and nutritional medicine;
pharmacology;
pharmacognosy;
toxicology;
epidemiology.

division.heading: Advisory Committee on Biologicals

content.p: The Advisory Committee on Biologicals is established.
The committee’s functions are, at the request of the Minister or Secretary, to provide advice and to make recommendations to the Minister or Secretary about one or more of the following matters:
the safety and efficacy of a biological;
the inclusion of a biological in the Register under Part 3-2A of the Act;
the variation of an entry for a biological included in the Register under Part 3-2A of the Act;
the continued retention of a biological in, or the removal of a biological from, the Register;
any other matter (whether or not related to a biological), including a matter related to standards.
The Minister or Secretary may require the committee to give its advice to other persons or bodies.
The Minister may, in writing, appoint up to 12 persons to the committee in accordance with subregulations (1A) and (1B).
Subject to subregulation (1B):
to the extent reasonably practicable, membership of the committee is to represent the widest possible range of fields mentioned in subregulation (2); and
each member of the committee must have expertise in at least one of those fields.
One member of the committee may have expertise in consumer health issues.
For the purposes of subregulation (1A), the fields are as follows:
infectious diseases;
tissue products;
blood products;
cellular therapies, including tissue engineering;
clinical expertise;
epidemiology or biostatistics;
toxicology.

division.heading: Advisory Committee on Vaccines

content.p: The Advisory Committee on Vaccines is established.
The committee’s functions are, at the request of the Minister or Secretary, to provide advice and to make recommendations to the Minister or Secretary about one or more of the following matters:
the safety, quality and efficacy of vaccines, including in relation to pharmacovigilance;
the registration of a vaccine;
the variation of an entry for a vaccine in the Register;
the continued retention of a vaccine in, or the removal of a vaccine from, the Register;
risk assessment and risk management of vaccines;
any other matter (whether or not related to a vaccine), including a matter related to standards.
The Minister or Secretary may require the committee to give its advice to other persons or bodies.
The Minister may, in writing, appoint up to 10 persons to the committee in accordance with subregulations (1A), (1B) and (2).
Subject to subregulations (1B) and (2):
to the extent reasonably practicable, membership of the committee is to represent the widest possible range of fields mentioned in subregulation (3); and
each member of the committee must have expertise in at least one of those fields.
One member of the committee may have expertise in consumer health issues.
The Minister may appoint one member from each of the following:
the Australian Technical Advisory Group on Immunisation;
the National Immunisation Committee;
the National Centre for Immunisation Research and Surveillance.
For the purposes of subregulation (1A), the fields are as follows:
immunology;
virology;
bacteriology;
infectious diseases in adults or children;
public health;
epidemiology or biostatistics;
vaccine program implementation;
the provision of immunisation treatment by an individual;
paediatrics;
nursing.

division.heading: General

content.p: This Division applies to committees mentioned in Divisions 1A, 1D, 1E, 1EA and 1EB.
A member is appointed to a committee for the term stated in the member’s instrument of appointment.
A term of appointment must not be longer than 3 years.
A member, other than a member mentioned in subregulation (4), must not be appointed for more than 3 consecutive terms.
A member appointed to a committee before the commencement of this subregulation must not be appointed for more than 3 further consecutive terms.
The Minister must appoint, in writing, a member of a committee to be its chair.
A member or chair may resign by giving written notice to the Minister.
If a chair ceases to be a member of a committee, the position is taken to be vacant.
The Minister may terminate a member’s appointment on any of the following grounds:
physical or mental incapacity;
misbehaviour;
incompetence;
bankruptcy;
failing to comply with the disclosure of interest requirements mentioned in regulation 42.
The Minister must terminate a member’s appointment if:
the member is convicted of an offence punishable by imprisonment for at least 1 year; or
if the member is absent without leave of absence from 3 consecutive meetings of the committee.
The Minister may grant leave of absence to the chair.
The chair may grant leave of absence to another committee member.
The Minister may appoint a person to act as a member of a committee.
A person may act as a member of a committee:
during a vacancy in the office, whether or not an appointment has previously been made to the office; or
during any period, or during all periods, when the holder of the office is absent from duty or is, for any reason, unable to perform the duties of the office.
A person appointed to act in an office must, to the extent reasonably practicable:
if a particular qualification is required for a substantive member—hold that qualification; or
if different qualifications are required for all members of the committee—hold 1 of those qualifications.
A person appointed to act during a vacancy must not continue to act for more than 12 months.
In performing its functions, a committee:
must act in accordance with this Division; and
must act with as little formality and as quickly as this Division and a proper consideration of the issues before the committee allow; and
is not bound by the rules of evidence; and
may obtain information about an issue in any way it considers appropriate (subject to subregulation 42(9)); and
may receive information or submissions orally or in writing; and

must comply with any directions given, in writing, to the committee by the Minister or the Secretary about the committee’s performance of its functions (other than a direction about advice given or proposed to be given by the committee).

The chair of a committee may give written notice to the committee, or to some members of the committee, directing the committee, or those members, to hold meetings at the times and places, and to deal with the matters in the manner, stated in the notice.
The procedure of a meeting must be determined by the committee in accordance with this Division.
The chair must preside at a committee meeting or nominate a member of the committee to preside at the meeting.
If the chair is temporarily absent from a meeting, the member chosen by the members present must preside at the meeting.
A member chosen to preside under subregulation (2) may exercise the powers and functions of the chair.
A quorum exists at a committee meeting when:
at least half of the members are present; or
at least half of the members who have been directed to hold the meeting under subregulation 41G(1) are present.
A decision made at a committee meeting by a majority of the votes of the members present and voting is a decision of the committee.
The member presiding at a committee meeting has a deliberative vote and, if the votes are equal, also has a casting vote.
Sitting fees and travel entitlements
A member of a committee is entitled to sitting fees and travel entitlements as determined by the Remuneration Tribunal.
When committee may establish subcommittees
A committee, with the approval of the Secretary, may establish subcommittees, consisting of members and other persons.
The function of the subcommittee is to inquire into, and report to the committee on, any matter referred to the subcommittee that is within the functions of the committee.
Disclosure of interests

A member of a committee who is aware that he or she has a direct or indirect material personal interest (whether pecuniary or not) in a matter being considered or about to be considered at a meeting of the committee must, without delay, disclose the nature of the interest at, or before, the meeting of the committee.

The disclosure must be recorded in the minutes of the meeting and the member must not, unless the committee otherwise determines, either be present during any deliberation of the committee about the matter or take part in any decision of the committee about that matter.

When a committee is making a determination about a member who has made a disclosure, the member, and any other member who has a direct or indirect material personal interest (whether pecuniary or not) in the matter to which the disclosure relates, must not either be present during any deliberation of the committee or take part in making the determination.

A member of a subcommittee appointed by a committee, who is aware that he or she has a direct or indirect material personal interest (whether pecuniary or not) in a matter being considered, or about to be considered, at a meeting of the subcommittee must, without delay, disclose the nature of the interest at, or before, the meeting of the subcommittee.
Seeking further advice
Any advice or recommendation given by a committee to the Minister or the Secretary may be given to another expert advisory committee for the advice of that committee.
In performing its functions, a committee may seek advice from other persons.
Validity of acts of members
Anything done by a person purporting to be or act as a member (including a chair) is not invalid because:
the person had not yet been appointed; or
there is a defect or irregularity in connection with the person’s appointment; or
the person’s appointment had ceased to have effect.
Records and reports
A committee must keep a record of its proceedings, and must prepare any other report about its activities that is requested by the Minister or the Secretary.
Publication of recommendations of committees
The Secretary must publish the recommendations of each committee.

division.heading: Advisory Committee on Medicines Scheduling

content.p: In this Division:
appointed member means a member of the Committee appointed by the Minister under subregulation 42ZCD(1).
Committee means the Advisory Committee on Medicines Scheduling.
Committee member means an appointed member or a nominated member.
nominated member means a member of the Committee nominated under subsection 52B(3) of the Act in accordance with regulation 42ZCE.
Note: The Committee is established by section 52B of the Act.
For subsection 52B(2) of the Act, the Committee is to be constituted in accordance with this Subdivision.
The Committee comprises each nominated member and no more than 8 appointed members.
A Committee member must have expertise in at least one of the following fields:
the regulation of scheduled medicines in Australia;
toxicology or pharmacology;
clinical pharmacology;
pharmacy practice;
medical practice;
consumer health issues relating to the regulation of therapeutic goods;
industry issues relating to the regulation of therapeutic goods.
Membership of the Committee must, to the extent reasonably practicable, represent the widest possible range of the fields mentioned in subregulation (2).
An appointed member must be appointed in writing by the Minister.
The term of an appointment of an appointed member is as specified in the instrument of appointment but must not be longer than 3 years.
An appointed member must not be appointed for more than 3 consecutive terms.
This regulation is made for subsection 52B(3) of the Act.
A nomination must be in writing.
The nomination must specify the term of the nominee’s membership of the Committee.
The nominee becomes a member of the Committee when the nomination is given to the Minister.
A nominated member stops being a member if:
the body that nominated the member gives the Minister written notice that the member’s nomination is withdrawn; or
the member, by written notice given to the Minister under subregulation 42ZCG(1), resigns from the Committee.

(6) The Commonwealth, each State, the Australian Capital Territory and the Northern Territory may, by written notice given to the Minister, nominate a member (the temporary nominee) to temporarily replace an existing member nominated by the Commonwealth, the State or Territory:
during a vacancy in the existing member’s office; or
during any period, or all periods, when the existing member is:
absent from duty or from Australia; or
for any other reason unable to perform the functions of a nominated member.
The temporary nominee becomes a member of the Committee, and the existing member stops being a member of the Committee:
when the circumstance giving rise to the temporary replacement commences; and
until that circumstance ends.

section.heading: Appointment of the Chair and acting Chair

content.p: The Minister must, in writing, appoint a Committee member to be the Chair of the Committee.
The Chair is appointed for the term stated in the appointment but may be reappointed for further terms.
The Minister may, in writing, appoint a Committee member to act as the Chair:
during a vacancy in the office of the Chair, whether or not an appointment has previously been made to the office; or
during any period, or during all periods, when the Chair is absent from duty or from Australia, or is, for any other reason, unable to perform the functions of the Chair.
Note: Section 33A of the Acts interpretation Act 1901 sets out various matters about acting appointments, including how long a person can act in a vacant office.
A Committee member or Chair may resign by giving written notice to the Minister.
If the Chair ceases to be a Committee member, the position is taken to be vacant.
The Minister may terminate an appointed member’s appointment on any of the following grounds:
physical or mental incapacity;
misbehaviour;
incompetence;
bankruptcy;
failing to comply with the disclosure of interest requirements mentioned in regulation 42ZCP.
The Minister must terminate an appointed member’s appointment if:
the member is convicted of an offence punishable by imprisonment for at least 1 year; or
if the member is absent without leave of absence from 3 consecutive meetings of the Committee.
The Minister may grant leave of absence to the Chair.
The Chair may grant leave of absence to a Committee member.
The Minister may, in writing, appoint a person to act as an appointed member:
during a vacancy in the office of an appointed member, whether or not an appointment has previously been made to the office; or
during any period, or during all periods, when an appointed member is absent from duty or from Australia, or is, for any reason, unable to perform the duties of the office.
A person appointed to act as an appointed member must have the expertise required for a substantive member.
Note: Section 33A of the Acts interpretation Act 1901 sets out various matters about acting appointments, including how long a person can act in a vacant office.
For subsection 52B(2) of the Act, the Committee is to hold meetings in accordance with this Subdivision.
The Chair of the Committee may give written notice to the Committee directing the Committee to hold meetings at the times and places, and to deal with the matters in the manner, stated in the notice.
The procedure of a meeting must be determined by the Committee in accordance with this Subdivision.
If the Chair of the Committee considers it appropriate and efficient in the circumstances, the Chair may direct the Committee to meet by video conference or teleconference or to meet out of session.
At a meeting, the Committee:
must act with as little formality and as quickly as this Subdivision and a proper consideration of the issues before the Committee allow; and
is not bound by the rules of evidence; and
may obtain information about an issue in any way it considers appropriate; and
may receive information in any way it considers appropriate; and

must comply with any directions given, in writing, to the Committee by the Minister or the Secretary about the Committee’s performance of its functions (other than a direction about advice given or proposed to be given by the Committee).
For this regulation:

out of session, in relation to a meeting, means a meeting in which the members take part by correspondence, email, telephone or in any other way that does not involve formal simultaneous meeting and voting.
The Chair must preside at a Committee meeting at which he or she is present.
If the Chair is unable to preside at a meeting, he or she must:
select a member of the Committee to preside at the meeting; and
advise the other Committee members of the selection.
If the Chair is temporarily absent from a meeting, the member chosen by the Committee members present must preside at the meeting.
A member presiding under subregulation (2) or (3) may exercise the powers and functions of the Chair.
A quorum exists at a Committee meeting when at least half of the Committee members are present.
A decision made at a Committee meeting by a majority of the votes of the members present and voting is a decision of the Committee.
Note: Decisions of the Committee relate to the recommendations and advice the Committee provides to the Secretary under subsection 52B(4) of the Act.
The member presiding at a Committee meeting has a deliberative vote and, if the votes are equal, also has a casting vote.
Sitting fees and travel entitlements
An appointed member is entitled to sitting fees and travel entitlements as determined by the Remuneration Tribunal.
When Committee may establish subcommittees
The Committee, with the approval of the Secretary, may establish subcommittees, consisting of Committee members and other persons.
The function of a subcommittee is to inquire into, and report to the Committee on, any matter referred to the subcommittee that is within the functions of the Committee.
Disclosure of interests

A Committee member who is aware that he or she has a direct or indirect material personal interest (whether pecuniary or not) in a matter being considered or about to be considered at a meeting of the Committee must, without delay, disclose the nature of the interest at, or before, the meeting of the Committee.

The disclosure must be recorded in the minutes of the meeting and the member must not, unless the Committee otherwise determines, either be present during any deliberation of the Committee about the matter or take part in any decision of the Committee about the matter.

When the Committee is making a determination about a member who has made a disclosure, the member, and any other member who has a direct or indirect material personal interest (whether pecuniary or not) in the matter to which the disclosure relates, must not be present during any deliberation of the Committee and must not take part in making the determination.

A member of a subcommittee appointed by the Committee, who is aware that he or she has a direct or indirect material personal interest (whether pecuniary or not) in a matter being considered, or about to be considered, at a meeting of the subcommittee must, without delay, disclose the nature of the interest at, or before, the meeting of the subcommittee.
Seeking and providing further advice
Any advice or recommendation given by the Committee to the Secretary may be given to another committee established under the Act or these Regulations for the advice of that committee.
In performing its functions, the Committee may seek advice from other persons.
Validity of acts of members
Anything done by a person purporting to be, or purporting to act as, a Committee member (including the Chair) is not invalid because:
the person had not yet been appointed; or
there is a defect or irregularity in connection with the person’s appointment; or
the person’s appointment had ceased to have effect.
Records and reports
The Committee must keep a record of its proceedings, and must prepare any other report about its activities that is requested by the Minister or the Secretary.
Publication
The Committee must publish details of any recommendations it makes.

division.heading: Advisory Committee on Chemicals Scheduling

appointed member means a member of the Committee appointed by the Minister under subregulation 42ZCT(1).
Committee means the Advisory Committee on Chemicals Scheduling.

nominated member means a member of the Committee nominated under subsection 52C(3) of the Act in accordance with regulation 42ZCU.

toxicology;

agricultural or veterinary chemicals;

section.heading: Appointment of the Chair and acting Chair

content.p: The Minister must, in writing, appoint a Committee member to be the Chair of the Committee.
The Chair is appointed for the term stated in the appointment but may be reappointed for further terms.
The Minister may, in writing, appoint a Committee member to act as the Chair:
during a vacancy in the office of the Chair, whether or not an appointment has previously been made to the office; or
during any period, or during all periods, when the Chair is absent from duty or from Australia, or is, for any other reason, unable to perform the functions of the Chair.
Note: Section 33A of the Acts interpretation Act 1901 sets out various matters about acting appointments, including how long a person can act in a vacant office.
A Committee member or Chair may resign by giving written notice to the Minister.
If the Chair ceases to be a Committee member, the position is taken to be vacant.
The Minister may terminate an appointed member’s appointment on any of the following grounds:
physical or mental incapacity;
misbehaviour;
incompetence;
bankruptcy;
failing to comply with the disclosure of interest requirements mentioned in regulation 42ZCZF.
The Minister must terminate an appointed member’s appointment if:
the member is convicted of an offence punishable by imprisonment for at least 1 year; or
if the member is absent without leave of absence from 3 consecutive meetings of the Committee.
The Minister may grant leave of absence to the Chair.
The Chair may grant leave of absence to a Committee member.
The Minister may, in writing, appoint a person to act as an appointed member:
during a vacancy in the office of an appointed member, whether or not an appointment has previously been made to the office; or
during any period, or during all periods, when an appointed member is absent from duty or from Australia, or is, for any reason, unable to perform the duties of the office.
A person appointed to act as an appointed member must have the expertise required for a substantive member.
Note: Section 33A of the Acts interpretation Act 1901 sets out various matters about acting appointments, including how long a person can act in a vacant office.
For subsection 52C(2) of the Act, the Committee is to hold meetings in accordance with this Subdivision.
The Chair of the Committee may give written notice to the Committee directing the Committee to hold meetings at the times and places, and to deal with the matters in the manner, stated in the notice.
The procedure of a meeting must be determined by the Committee in accordance with this Subdivision.
If the Chair of the Committee considers it appropriate and efficient in the circumstances, the Chair may direct the Committee to meet by video conference or teleconference or to meet out of session.
At a meeting, the Committee:
must act with as little formality and as quickly as this Subdivision and a proper consideration of the issues before the Committee allow; and
is not bound by the rules of evidence; and
may obtain information about an issue in any way it considers appropriate; and
may receive information in any way it considers appropriate; and

must comply with any directions given, in writing, to the Committee by the Minister or the Secretary about the Committee’s performance of its functions (other than a direction about advice given or proposed to be given by the Committee).
For this regulation:

out of session, in relation to a meeting, means a meeting in which the members take part by correspondence, email, telephone or in any other way that does not involve formal simultaneous meeting and voting.
The Chair must preside at a Committee meeting at which he or she is present.
If the Chair is unable to preside at a meeting, he or she must:
select a member of the Committee to preside at the meeting; and
advise the other Committee members of the selection.
If the Chair is temporarily absent from a meeting, the member chosen by the Committee members present must preside at the meeting.
A member presiding under subregulation (2) or (3) may exercise the powers and functions of the Chair.
A quorum exists at a Committee meeting when at least half of the Committee members are present.
A decision made at a Committee meeting by a majority of the votes of the members present and voting is a decision of the Committee.
Note: Decisions of the Committee relate to the recommendations and advice the Committee provides to the Secretary under subsection 52C(4) of the Act.
The member presiding at a Committee meeting has a deliberative vote and, if the votes are equal, also has a casting vote.
Sitting fees and travel entitlements
An appointed member is entitled to sitting fees and travel entitlements as determined by the Remuneration Tribunal.
When Committee may establish subcommittees
The Committee, with the approval of the Secretary, may establish subcommittees, consisting of Committee members and other persons.
The function of the subcommittee is to inquire into, and report to the Committee on, any matter referred to the subcommittee that is within the functions of the Committee.
Disclosure of interests

A Committee member who is aware that he or she has a direct or indirect material personal interest (whether pecuniary or not) in a matter being considered or about to be considered at a meeting of the Committee must, without delay, disclose the nature of the interest at, or before, the meeting of the Committee.

The disclosure must be recorded in the minutes of the meeting and the member must not, unless the Committee otherwise determines, either be present during any deliberation of the Committee about the matter or take part in any decision of the Committee about the matter.

When the Committee is making a determination about a member who has made a disclosure, the member, and any other member who has a direct or indirect material personal interest (whether pecuniary or not) in the matter to which the disclosure relates, must not be present during any deliberation of the Committee and must not take part in making the determination.

A member of a subcommittee appointed by the Committee, who is aware that he or she has a direct or indirect material personal interest (whether pecuniary or not) in a matter being considered, or about to be considered, at a meeting of the subcommittee must, without delay, disclose the nature of the interest at, or before, the meeting of the subcommittee.
Seeking and providing further advice
Any advice or recommendation given by the Committee to the Secretary may be given to another committee established under the Act or these Regulations for the advice of that committee.
In performing its functions, the Committee may seek advice from other persons.
Validity of acts of members
Anything done by a person purporting to be, or purporting to act as, a Committee member (including the Chair) is not invalid because:
the person had not yet been appointed; or
there is a defect or irregularity in connection with the person’s appointment; or
the person’s appointment had ceased to have effect.
Records and reports
The Committee must keep a record of its proceedings, and must prepare any other report about its activities that is requested by the Minister or the Secretary.
Publication
The Committee must publish details of any recommendations it makes.

division.heading: Joint meetings

content.p: For section 52CA of the Act, the Advisory Committee on Medicines Scheduling and the Advisory Committee on Chemicals Scheduling may hold joint meetings in accordance with this Division.

The Secretary may, if the Secretary considers it appropriate to do so, give written notice to the Committee members of both Committees directing the Committees to hold a joint meeting at the time and place, and to deal with the matters in the manner, stated in the notice.
At a joint meeting, the Committee members present at the meeting must vote on which Chair (or presiding member) is to be the Chair of the joint meeting.
For the purpose of choosing a Chair, a Committee member may cast one vote in respect of each Committee of which he or she is a member.
There is a quorum at a joint meeting if there is a quorum for each Committee.
At a joint meeting:
decisions are to be made by a majority of the votes cast by the members present and voting; and
each member has one vote in respect of each Committee of which he or she is a member.
A decision made at a joint meeting is taken to be a decision of each Committee for the purposes of any advice or recommendation provided to the Secretary by either Committee.
Note: Decisions at a joint meeting relate to the recommendations and advice a Committee may provide to the Secretary under subsections 52B(4) and 52C(4) of the Act.
Each Committee must keep a record of the proceedings of the joint meeting.

division.heading: Procedure for amending the current Poisons Standard

content.p: In this Division:
business day means a day that is not a Saturday, Sunday or public holiday in the Australian Capital Territory.
Committee member means a member of: the Advisory Committee on Medicines Scheduling; or the Advisory Committee on Chemicals Scheduling.
the Advisory Committee on Medicines Scheduling; or
the Advisory Committee on Chemicals Scheduling.
expert advisory committee means:
the Advisory Committee on Medicines Scheduling; or
the Advisory Committee on Chemicals Scheduling; or
the Advisory Committee on Medicines Scheduling and the Advisory Committee on Chemicals Scheduling in joint session.
first closing date has the meaning given by paragraph 42ZCZK(1)(d).
interim decision means:
in Subdivision 3D.2—a decision of the Secretary under regulation 42ZCZN; and
in Subdivision 3D.3—a decision of the Secretary under paragraph 42ZCZV(a).

proposed amendment means a proposal to amend the current Poisons Standard under subsection 52D(2) of the Act on the Secretary’s own initiative or in response to an application under section 52EAA of the Act.
public submission means a submission under this Division by a person who is not a Committee member.
relevant submission has the meaning given by paragraph 42ZCZQ(1)(a).
second closing date has the meaning given by paragraph 42ZCZP(1)(c).
Note: For current Poisons Standard see s 52A of the Act.

subDivision.heading: Procedure if proposed amendment referred to expert advisory committee

content.p: For subsection 52D(2) of the Act, this Subdivision sets out the procedure that is to be followed in amending the current Poisons Standard:
if:
a person applies to the Secretary under section 52EAA of the Act to amend the current Poisons Standard; and
the Secretary decides to refer the proposed amendment to an expert advisory committee; or
if the Secretary decides:
to amend the current Poisons Standard on his or her own initiative; and
to refer the proposed amendment to an expert advisory committee.
Note: This Subdivision does not limit the way the Secretary may exercise a power under subsection 52D(2) of the Act in other circumstances.

section.heading: Proposed amendment to be referred to expert advisory committee

content.p: The Secretary must publish, in a manner the Secretary considers appropriate, a notice:
specifying the expert advisory committee to which the proposed amendment will be referred; and
specifying the date of the meeting of the committee; and
setting out details of the proposed amendment; and
(d) inviting public submissions to be made to the committee by a date mentioned in the notice as the closing date for public submissions (the first closing date).
The first closing date must be at least 20 business days after publication of the notice.
The date of the meeting must be at least 10 business days after the first closing date.
At a meeting of an expert advisory committee to consider the proposed amendment, the committee must consider all public submissions received by the first closing date that:
address a matter mentioned in section 52E of the Act; and
are relevant to the proposed amendment.
The committee is not required to consider a public submission received after the first closing date.
Subject to subregulation (4), the Secretary must publish, in a manner the Secretary considers appropriate, all public submissions received on or before the first closing date.
The Secretary must not publish any information that the Secretary considers to be confidential information.
After consideration of any public submissions received, the expert advisory committee must provide advice or a recommendation to the Secretary in relation to the proposed amendment.
After considering the advice or recommendation of the expert advisory committee, the Secretary must, subject to regulation 42ZCZO, make an interim decision in relation to the proposed amendment.

section.heading: Secretary may make final decision if no interim decision required

content.p: The Secretary may make a final decision without making an interim decision if no public submissions are received in response to an invitation under paragraph 42ZCZK(1)(d).
The Secretary must comply with regulation 42ZCZS after making the final decision.
As soon as practicable after making the interim decision, the Secretary must publish, in a manner the Secretary considers appropriate, a notice:
setting out the interim decision and the reasons for making the interim decision; and
if the interim decision is to amend the current Poisons Standard—specifying the proposed date of effect of the proposed amendment; and

(c) inviting interested persons to make submissions to the Secretary in relation to the interim decision by a date mentioned in the notice as the closing date for submissions (the second closing date); and

if the interim decision is in response to an application made under section 52EAA—inviting the person who made the application to make a submission in relation to the interim decision by the second closing date.
The second closing date must be at least 10 business days after publication of the notice.
If the Secretary receives further submissions on or before the second closing date, the Secretary must, as soon as practicable after the second closing date:
(a) consider all public submissions (the relevant submissions) made by the second closing date that:
address a matter mentioned in section 52E of the Act; and
are relevant to the Secretary’s interim decision; and
reconsider the interim decision in light of those submissions and any advice received in response to a request under paragraph (2)(a).
In reconsidering the interim decision, the Secretary:
may request advice from any committee or any person; and
is not required to engage in further public consultation.
The Secretary need not consider a public submission made after the second closing date.
Subject to subsection (5), the Secretary must publish, in a manner the Secretary considers appropriate, all relevant submissions.
The Secretary must not publish any information that the Secretary considers to be confidential information.

section.heading: Final decision if there is an interim decision

content.p: The Secretary may make a final decision by confirming, varying or setting aside the interim decision only:
after considering all relevant submissions and any advice received in response to a request under paragraph 42ZCZQ(2)(a); or
if there are no such submissions or advice.
After making a final decision under regulation 42ZCZR or 42ZCZO, the Secretary must:
publish, in a manner that the Secretary considers appropriate:
the decision; and
the reasons for the decision; and
the date of effect of the decision; and
if the decision is to amend the current Poisons Standard—make the amendment.
Note: The Secretary must comply with section 52E of the Act when amending the current Poisons Standard.

subDivision.heading: Procedure if proposed amendments not referred to expert advisory committee

content.p: This Subdivision applies if the Secretary:
receives an application under section 52EAA of the Act to amend the current Poisons Standard; and
decides not to refer the proposed amendment to an expert advisory committee.
